How New Species Evolve
¨Macroevolutionis best observed within the fossil record.
¤Shows evolution on a large scale
¨Involves speciation.
¤Splitting of one species into 2 or more new species
¤Macroevolution is the result of accumulation of microevolutions that result in formation of new species
¨Every species has its own evolutionary history
¤Species concept –Refers to the different ways in which a species is defined
¤Taxonomistsanalyze and define species
explanation: Macroevolution refers to evolution on a large scale, which is best observed within the fossil record. It involves speciation, defined as the splitting of one species into two or more new species. Macroevolution occurs as a result of the gradual accumulation of many microevolutionary changes over time. Every species has its own distinct evolutionary history. Because defining species can be complex, scientists use different 'species concepts' (the various ways species are defined), and taxonomists are the specialists who analyze and define these species groups.

questions.q: What is macroevolution, and where is it best observed?
opts: Small-scale allele changes observed in lab bacteria
Large-scale evolutionary changes best observed in the fossil record
The random mating patterns of island finches
Artificial selection performed by human breeders
questions.exp: The notes define macroevolution as evolution on a large scale, which is best observed in the fossil record.

questions.q: How is speciation defined on this page?
opts: The movement of alleles between separate populations
The splitting of one species into two or more new species
The maintenance of stable allele frequencies
The classification of fossils based on age
questions.exp: Speciation is defined on the slide as the 'splitting of one species into 2 or more new species.'
